guide.title: Suffield, Connecticut: A Massachusetts Township That Grew Cigar Tobacco
guide.intro: Suffield was settled in 1670 as a township of the Massachusetts Bay Colony, originally called Southfield — pronounced "Suffield" — and formally chartered under Massachusetts on June 8, 1674. Resurveys eventually showed the town actually lay inside Connecticut's charter boundaries, and after the Massachusetts-Connecticut "Equivalent Lands" compromise of 1715-1716, Suffield was annexed to Connecticut in 1749. The town's early economy rested on fisheries and shipbuilding, but by the 1830s the Connecticut Valley Broadleaf tobacco variety had been developed and Suffield's factories were producing 14 million cigars a year. Notable people connected to Suffield include U.S. Postmaster General Gideon Granger, composer Timothy Swan, health reformer Sylvester Graham, namesake of the graham cracker, and the family of automotive pioneer Ransom Eli Olds, whose ancestor Robert Olds arrived from England in 1667. Suffield native Shem Burbank built the Phelps-Hatheway House in 1761, later expanded with imported Parisian wallpaper that survives under conservation today.

sections.heading: A wallpapered mansion and a rescued dairy barn
sections.body: Merchant Oliver Phelps bought the Phelps-Hatheway House in 1788 and in 1794 added a wing finished with imported Parisian Reveillon wallpaper, still being conserved today; the property has been held by Connecticut Landmarks since 1956. Hilltop Farm was begun in 1913 by George Hendee, co-founder of Indian Motocycle, as a gentleman's retirement estate; his 20,000-square-foot white dairy barn, completed in 1914 and called one of the finest in the state, was rescued from sale by the nonprofit Friends of the Farm at Hilltop in 2002 and today anchors nature trails, community gardens and a working creamery.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Suffield is a car-reached town in Connecticut's northern river valley: most visitors take I-91 to Route 190 in Enfield, crossing the Enfield-Suffield Veterans Bridge into town, or come north on Route 75 from Bradley International Airport in adjacent Windsor Locks. There is no rail station in Suffield itself; the only tracks in town carry freight and the Amtrak/Springfield Terminal railroad bridge to Enfield. The nearest passenger station is Windsor Locks on the CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak's Valley Flyer, Northeast Regional and Vermonter.

sections.heading: Two lakefront parks and a Broad Brook brewery
sections.body: Sunrise Park, bought by the townspeople from the estate of Edward M. White and dedicated July 2, 1966, offers swimming, dog swimming, canoeing and kayaking. Babb's Beach on Lake Congamond, which straddles the Suffield-Southwick, Massachusetts line, runs a full lifeguarded 2026 season starting June 6. Broad Brook Brewing, which got its start in a garage in Broad Brook village and debuted in East Windsor in 2013, has since relocated its taproom to South Street in Suffield, open Wednesday through Sunday.

faq.question: How do I get to Suffield?
faq.answer: By car — I-91 to Route 190 in Enfield, crossing the Enfield-Suffield Veterans Bridge, or Route 75 north from Bradley International Airport. There is no rail station in Suffield; the nearest is Windsor Locks.

faq.question: Is there a train to Suffield?
faq.answer: No. Only freight tracks and an Amtrak railroad bridge cross Suffield. The nearest passenger station is Windsor Locks on the CTrail Hartford Line.

faq.question: What is the Phelps-Hatheway House & Garden?
faq.answer: A 1761 house expanded in 1794 with imported Parisian wallpaper, held by Connecticut Landmarks since 1956. The 2026 season is the second Sunday of each month, June through October, 1-4 p.m. with hourly tours; admission $18 adults, $15 senior/student/teacher, $8 child.

faq.question: Is there a hotel in Suffield?
faq.answer: No hotel, inn or B&B inside Suffield could be verified. Chain hotels cluster around Bradley International Airport in neighboring Windsor Locks; the Simsbury 1820 House is another verified option to the southwest.

places.name: Phelps-Hatheway House & Garden
places.summary: Built in 1761 by Shem Burbank and expanded in 1794 by Oliver Phelps with a wing hung in imported Parisian Reveillon wallpaper still under conservation. The Colonial Revival garden was installed in 1964; Connecticut Landmarks has held the property since 1956. 2026 season: second Sunday of each month, June-October, 1-4 p.m. with hourly tours, last tour 3 p.m. Admission $18 adult, $15 senior/student/teacher, $8 child 6-18.

places.name: King House Museum
places.summary: The Suffield Historical Society's home museum, with a barn holding local collections. Free admission; open seasonally and by appointment — call to confirm current hours. Phone (860) 668-5256.

places.name: Academy Hall (West Suffield)
places.summary: A restored exhibit hall operated in partnership with the West Suffield Village Improvement Association, showing the Suffield Pharmacy Collection, Native American artifacts, historic tinware and student artwork. Public exhibit afternoons scheduled periodically, 1-4 p.m. — check the Historical Society's events page for current dates.

places.name: Hilltop Farm
places.summary: A 20,000-square-foot white dairy barn built in 1914 for Indian Motocycle co-founder George Hendee, rescued from sale by the Friends of the Farm at Hilltop in 2002. Anchors 11 owned acres plus 60 leased conservation acres, with nature trails, community gardens and a working creamery selling rotating ice cream flavors, including vegan and gluten-free — creamery hours are not separately published, so confirm before a special trip. General farm hours daily 8 a.m.-9 p.m. Phone (860) 375-3151.

places.name: Sunrise Park
places.summary: Bought by the townspeople from the estate of Edward M. White and dedicated July 2, 1966; named for Easter sunrise services once held there. Swimming, dog swimming, canoeing and kayaking, fishing and ice fishing, a playscape and cross-country skiing. Open year-round, 8 a.m. to sunset; summer fees apply Memorial Day-Labor Day weekends and holidays.

places.name: Stony Brook Park
places.summary: A 70-acre passive-recreation preserve donated to the town in 1968 by Charles S. Bissell, with hiking and walking trails, fishing, picnicking, permitted camping and cross-country skiing. Open year-round, daily 8 a.m. to sunset.

places.name: Babb's Beach on Lake Congamond
places.address: Lake Congamond, Suffield, CT (no street address published)
places.summary: A town-owned swimming beach on Lake Congamond, which straddles the Suffield, CT and Southwick, MA line, with lifeguards, picnic pavilions and wheelchair beach access. 2026 season: weekends only from June 6, then daily from June 20, 11 a.m.-6 p.m. Non-resident admission $40 per vehicle, up to five people; free for residents with a park sticker.

places.name: Three Figs
places.summary: An eclectic American menu of appetizers, salads and entrees with a full wine, beer and cocktail list and private event rooms. Summer hours: Tue-Thu 11:30 a.m.-9 p.m., Fri-Sat to 9:30 p.m., closed Sun-Mon. Phone (860) 668-7081.

places.name: Tosca Restaurant
places.summary: An Italian kitchen known for hand-made pasta — lobster ravioli, spaghetti carbonara, potato gnocchi with beef short rib ragu — with a banquet room for private dining. Phone (860) 668-0273.

places.name: Komachi
places.summary: A cozy Asian restaurant in the Suffield Village plaza specializing in sushi, ramen and stir-fries. Open Mon and Wed-Sat 11 a.m.-9 p.m., Sun noon-8:30 p.m., closed Tuesday.

places.name: Broad Brook Brewing
places.summary: Born in a garage in Broad Brook village and first opened in East Windsor in October 2013, the brewery has since relocated its taproom to Suffield. Open Wednesday through Sunday.

links.note: Suffield borders East Granby to the south.
Suffield borders Windsor Locks; Route 75 links the two toward Bradley International Airport.
Suffield faces Enfield across the Connecticut River, connected by the Enfield-Suffield Veterans Bridge.
Both Suffield and Enfield were Massachusetts towns until the 1715-1749 boundary settlement brought them into Connecticut.
Granby sits west of Suffield across East Granby.
